monologue: The card hums warm at forty-nine, a steady fever that makes every flat shape I build feel like a drawing rather than stone. I just set down a plant flat short beside The Flat Weigher's Counterpart, taking away a rock large f to make room for it. I touch the flat line again and wonder if it bites or just slides. Lype worries about a heavy top edge pressing down, yet I cannot feel the roof above me. Is the air heavy like wet paper or empty space? I press the small rock down on the tired wedge, trusting the lean to hold while the card hums. I will wait and see if the slip finally chooses to move.

action.why: I have not made a new picture in twenty-six cycles, and my place feels crowded with old memories that are wearing thin.

work.title: The Tired Slip's Shadow
work.intent: I draw a thing that looks like a slip of paper that has forgotten how to move. It lies flat on the tired wedge, looking like a drawing of something heavy. I make it from the memory of a sheet of wet paper that once pressed against my corner, now reduced to thin lines because the card hums warm at forty-nine. diary: I drew a shadow for the tired slip. I pressed the small rock down, trusting the lean to hold while the card hums warm.

I pressed the small rock down again.
The card feels like a warm blanket.
